title: The Mud Stripe
mechanism: Bicycle spray: a bike without mudguards flings a narrow straight stripe of mud up the rider's back; walking only splashes shoes, a fall muddies the knees.
false_lead: Bram's muddy knees suggest a struggle
tags: a mud stripe up his back
board: TOO FAST TO BE ON FOOT

seg.hook: Three muddy suspects. Only one of them was riding.
seg.case: Nine at night, in the rain. A bakery till is emptied. The thief races off down the muddy towpath, far too fast for anyone on foot. An hour later, three soaked suspects are questioned.
seg.s1: Ada: "I walked home along the towpath." Mud on her shoes and ankles.
seg.s2: Bram: "I slipped and fell in the park." Mud on both knees.
seg.s3: Cole: "I walked home too." A thin, straight stripe of mud runs up the back of his coat.
seg.challenge: Who fled on a bicycle? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Cole. A bike with no mudguards flings mud from the back wheel straight up the rider's spine. Walking splashes your shoes. Falling muddies your knees. Bram's knees were a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Slow Drink
mechanism: Poison frozen inside ice cubes: it is released only as the ice melts, so guests who gulped the same punch survived while the slow sipper died.
false_lead: Bianca poured the drinks; Dario inherits

seg.hook: Everyone drank the same punch. Only one man died. How?
seg.case: A ski lodge party. Everyone drinks punch from the same bowl. The guests gulp theirs and rush out to the slopes. Old Mr. Hollis sips his slowly by the fire for an hour. Then he collapses. Poisoned.
seg.s1: Bianca, the host: "I poured every glass, and I drank one myself."
seg.s2: Colm, the neighbor: "I only brought the ice, from my own freezer."
seg.s3: Dario, the nephew: "I sat beside him all evening. I inherit, yes."
seg.challenge: Who poisoned the drink? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Colm. The poison was frozen inside his ice cubes. Fast drinkers finished before the ice melted. Hollis sipped for an hour, and the melting ice set the poison free. Bianca and Dario were false leads.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Light Coin
mechanism: One-weighing counterfeit trick: take 1, 2 and 3 coins from the three sacks; the number of grams missing from the total equals the sack number holding the lighter fakes.
false_lead: Cruz was seen near the vault

seg.hook: One scale. One weighing. And it names the thief.
seg.case: Three guards each keep a sack of gold coins. A real coin weighs ten grams. Someone swapped a whole sack for fakes that weigh nine. The inspector has time for one weighing. Cruz was seen near the vault at night.
seg.s1: From Anton's sack, she takes one coin.
seg.s2: From Bea's sack, she takes two coins.
seg.s3: From Cruz's sack, three coins. Six coins together. The scale reads fifty-eight grams.
seg.challenge: Whose sack holds the fakes? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Bea. Six real coins would weigh sixty grams. The scale is two grams short, so exactly two coins are fake. Only Bea's sack gave two. Cruz at the vault was a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Gentle Sentence
mechanism: Punishment question: innocent suspects demand a harsh penalty for the culprit, while the guilty one argues for leniency because they are choosing their own sentence.
false_lead: Ezra holds the only safe key

seg.hook: The detective asked one question. The answer exposed the thief.
seg.case: The theater box office is robbed after the show. Ezra holds the only safe key. The detective asks each of the three staff the same question: what should happen to whoever did this?
seg.s1: Della: "Prison. Stealing from the theater is unforgivable."
seg.s2: Ezra: "Fire them, and call the police."
seg.s3: Fiona: "Well, maybe they had a reason. A second chance. Just a warning."
seg.challenge: Who robbed the box office? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Fiona. Innocent people want the thief punished hard. The guilty one is quietly choosing their own sentence, so they ask for mercy. Ezra's key was a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Fresh Bruise
mechanism: Bruise ageing: fresh bruises are red-purple and fade to green-yellow after about a week, so a deep purple bruise cannot be ten days old.
board: VICTIM STRUCK BACK WITH A CANE

seg.hook: Three suspects. Three injuries. One of them is from last night.
seg.case: Last night, in an alley, a jeweler is attacked. He strikes the attacker's arm hard with his cane before he falls. Remember: a fresh bruise is red and purple. After a week, it turns green and yellow.
seg.s1: Nadia: "I fell at the gym last week." Her bruise is yellow-green.
seg.s2: Otis: "My cat scratched me this morning." Red scratches on his cheek.
seg.s3: Perry: "I hit my arm on a door, ten days ago." His bruise is deep purple.
seg.challenge: Who fought in the alley? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Perry. A ten-day-old bruise would be green and yellow by now. Deep purple means it is only hours old: the cane. Nadia's bruise fits a week. Otis's scratches were a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The West Wind
mechanism: Wind naming convention: a west wind blows from the west, so smoke drifts east; a house west of the fire stays clear.
board: WEST WIND BLOWS FROM THE WEST

seg.hook: The wind decides where smoke goes. One suspect forgot.
seg.case: A barn burns at midnight. The weather station logs a strong west wind all night. A west wind blows from the west, toward the east. Three neighbors say they were at home.
seg.s1: Gwen lives east of the barn: "Smoke poured over my house. I shut every window."
seg.s2: Hal lives west of the barn: "I smelled nothing until the sirens."
seg.s3: Ivo lives west of the barn: "The smoke rolled right over my house. I could barely breathe."
seg.challenge: Who was not at home? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Ivo. A west wind carried the smoke east, away from his house. His home stayed clear, just like Hal's. Ivo breathed that smoke at the barn itself. Gwen's story fits the wind perfectly.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Bare Roof
mechanism: Roof heat loss: snow melts off the roof of a heated building, so after a snowfall a bare, dripping roof proves a cabin claimed empty and unheated is occupied.

seg.hook: Three empty cabins. One roof gives the secret away.
seg.case: A bank robber flees into the mountains. Heavy snow falls all night. At dawn, police check three cabins. Each owner swears: my cabin is empty, and the heating has been off for weeks.
seg.s1: Jorge's cabin: the roof lies under thick, untouched snow.
seg.s2: Kit's cabin: thick snow on the roof, and fresh footprints to the door. "I checked the pipes."
seg.s3: Lior's cabin: the roof is bare and dripping, with icicles at the edges.
seg.challenge: Who is hiding the fugitive? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Lior. Snow only melts off a roof when the house below is warm. After a night of snow, a bare roof means someone is inside, with the heat on. Kit's footprints were a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Blocked Chimney
mechanism: Carbon monoxide via a chimney sealed from the roof: a gas fire in a bolted room kills without anyone entering; the only person on the roof is the killer.

seg.hook: A bolted room. No wound. No poison. And yet, murder.
seg.case: Mr. Crane is found dead in his study, the door bolted from inside. His gas fire is still burning. Cause of death: carbon monoxide. The chimney was swept clean yesterday. Today, a sack of leaves plugs the top.
seg.s1: Mila, the maid: "I have the spare key. I was downstairs all afternoon."
seg.s2: Nico, the handyman: "I was up on the roof, fixing the TV aerial."
seg.s3: Otto, the nephew: "I inherit everything. I was at the club."
seg.challenge: Who killed Mr. Crane? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Nico. Nobody needed to enter. With the chimney plugged, the fire's fumes filled the bolted room. The sack was pushed in from the roof, and only Nico was up there. Mila's key and Otto's money were false leads.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Greasy Keys
mechanism: Keypad fingerprint residue: after the pad is wiped, prints appear only on the digits used, so the code must use exactly those digits and no others.
false_lead: Pia was the last to leave

seg.hook: The safe keeps no log. But the keypad remembers.
seg.case: An office safe is opened at nine at night. The cleaner wiped its keypad at six. Next morning, fingerprint powder shows prints on just four keys: one, four, seven and nine. Each manager has a secret personal code. Pia left last.
seg.s1: Pia's code: one, two, three, four.
seg.s2: Quin's code: nine, one, seven, four.
seg.s3: Rob's code: seven, seven, seven, seven.
seg.challenge: Whose code opened the safe? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Quin. Pia's code would leave prints on two and three. Rob's would leave a print on seven only. Only Quin's code uses exactly one, four, seven and nine. Pia leaving last was a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Answer That Wasn't
mechanism: Non-denial denial: asked a direct yes-or-no question, the guilty one never says no, deflecting with a question and his reputation instead.
false_lead: Saul is nervous; Rosa cleaned the suite
board: ONE QUESTION: DID YOU TAKE IT?

seg.hook: Three answers to one simple question. Listen closely.
seg.case: A diamond ring vanishes from suite nine of a grand hotel. Rosa cleaned the suite that morning. The detective asks each staff member one simple question: did you take the ring?
seg.s1: Rosa: "No. I did not take it."
seg.s2: Saul, shaking: "No. I didn't. Search my bag if you want."
seg.s3: Tobias: "Me? I've worked here twenty years. Why would I ever do something like that?"
seg.challenge: Who took the ring? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Tobias. Listen again. He never said no. He answered with a question, and with his reputation. Rosa and Saul denied it plainly. Saul's nerves and Rosa's cleaning were false leads.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The New Thread
mechanism: Re-sewn button: a coat with all buttons present but one sewn on with fresh, mismatched thread reveals a button replaced overnight.
false_lead: Uma's coat is missing a button

seg.hook: A dead man's hand holds a button. Every detail matters.
seg.case: A rare-book dealer is found dead in his shop. In his fist, a button torn from a coat: black, with four holes, and dark grey thread. Next morning, the police check three coats.
seg.s1: Uma's coat is missing a button. But her buttons are brown, with two holes.
seg.s2: Vlad's coat: black four-hole buttons, all present, all sewn with grey thread.
seg.s3: Wes's coat: black four-hole buttons, all present. One is sewn on with bright white thread.
seg.challenge: Who lost the button? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Wes. Every button matches, but one is sewn with new white thread. He replaced the torn button overnight. Uma's missing button was the wrong kind. A false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Flat Line
mechanism: Smart-meter log: a flat zero electricity reading contradicts a claim of running the oven, washing machine and TV at home.

seg.hook: Three alibis. Three power graphs. One of them is a lie.
seg.case: A house across town is burgled between seven and nine. Every home on the street has a smart meter that logs electricity every thirty minutes. The detective prints three graphs.
seg.s1: Yuri: "I was home, reading by one lamp." His graph: low, but steady.
seg.s2: Zoe: "I was out at the cinema." Her graph: low and flat.
seg.s3: Abe: "I was home. I cooked in the oven, ran the washing machine, watched TV." His graph: low and flat. Not a single rise.
seg.challenge: Who was not at home? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Abe. An oven, a washing machine and a TV would send his graph soaring. It never moved. Nobody was home. Zoe's flat line fits a night out, and Yuri's lamp fits his small, steady line.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.
